title: Jeffery Johnson
description: Jeffery Lynn Johnson had to close his toolbox for the last time on 15 March 2024. Born 23 July in Belmond, Jeffery did a lot of work with his family's paint and gift store in Clear Lake where he…
content:
Jeffery Lynn Johnson had to close his toolbox for the last time on 15 March 2024.
Born 23 July in Belmond, Jeffery did a lot of work with his family's paint and gift store in Clear Lake where he learned his lifelong hard work ethic. Shortly after graduating from Clear Lake High School he started his adventures with his best friend, Ed Peck, as he developed memories of extreme adventures through most of the lower 48 from Jackson Hole to Alabama that he would share while reminiscing the rest of his life. His adventures eventually led him to Alaska in 1983. It was the start of developing his love of Lake Louise in 1985 when he began building his log cabin with his father Merlin Johnson. He built many strong friendships and helped with so many work and personal projects that his handiwork in construction can be seen throughout Alaska, even as far as the southern-most island of Honolulu, Hawaii.
He is survived by his brother Randy, his nephew Brian, niece Laura, and many dear family members in Iowa, as well as friends Ashley, Brittany, Ed, Jack, Lon, Russ, Shelly, Bob and Tom and so many more. Jeff will make his final trip to the cabin he built in March 2025. Jeff kept notes to always remember all his beloved friends and family, so in lieu of flowers or donations, call a friend and meet them; cherish your friends as much as Jeff cherished his. Category:

title: Marlin Miller
description: Marlin 'Pee Wee' Eugene Miller, 88, died Monday, June 24, 2024 at the IOOF Home in Mason City. A funeral service was held at 11:00 a.m., Friday June 28, 2024, at the Fertile Church of Christ, with…
content:
Marlin 'Pee Wee' Eugene Miller, 88, died Monday, June 24, 2024 at the IOOF Home in Mason City.
A funeral service was held at 11:00 a.m., Friday June 28, 2024, at the Fertile Church of Christ, with Rev. Ken Olson officiating. Burial took place at Memorial Park Cemetery, Mason City. Visitation was held one hour prior to the service at the church.
Memorials may be directed to the family in Marlin's memory.
Marlin Eugene Miller was born on March 26, 1936, in rural Clear Lake, the son of Verle F. and Corrine (Zobel) Miller. Marlin was a graduate of Fertile High School in the class of 1954. He operated the service station in Fertile for several years. Marlin's work experience also included working at Sears in Mason City, Miller's Diesel and lastly Opportunity Village.
Marlin was married to Elizabeth Caffrey; they were blessed with two children Rhonda and Jeff.
On December 13, 1974, Marlin was united in marriage to Dianne Kay Ouverson at the Fertile Church of Christ. They made their home in Clear Lake. Marlin was a member of the Church of Christ where he was a deacon, Sunday School teacher and sang in the choir. He was a member of the North Iowa Road Riders for several years.
Marlin enjoyed taking fishing trips with his father Verle and his brothers, Earl and Jack. Other interests of Marlin's were watching Westerns, NASCAR races and taking motorcycle trips. Louis L'Amour was one of his favorite authors and he greatly loved music. In retirement, Marlin delighted in being a snowbird to southern Texas.
Marlin is survived by his wife Dianne Miller of Clear Lake; son, Jeffrey (Mary) Miller; grandchildren, Tara (Dan) Lincicum, April (Dan) Guffey, Jamie Miller, Bryan (Tammy) Miller, Mark Miller; 11 great-grandchildren; sister, Jean (Dan) Blake; sisters-in-law Donna and Eva Miller; along with other relatives and friends.
Marlin is preceded in death by his parents, Verle and Corrine Miller; daughter, Rhonda E. (Phillip) Krambeer; brothers, Earl and Jack Miller; nephews Jack Jr. Miller and Jerry Gudmonson.
Ward Van Slyke is in charge of arrangements.

title: Donna A. Miller
description: Donna A. Miller, 91, passed away surrounded by her loving family on Friday, February 21, 2025, in Clear Lake. A funeral service will be held at 10:30 a.m., Friday, February 28, 2025, at the Fertile…
content:
Donna A. Miller, 91, passed away surrounded by her loving family on Friday, February 21, 2025, in Clear Lake.
A funeral service will be held at 10:30 a.m., Friday, February 28, 2025, at the Fertile Church of Christ, 3493 Eagle Ave., Fertile; with her son, Pastor Daniel Miller officiating. Burial will take place at Memorial Park Cemetery in Mason City.
A viewing will be held Thursday, February 27, 2025, at Ward Van Slyke Colonial Chapel, 310 First Ave. North, Clear Lake. Memorials may be directed to a charity of choice in Donna's memory.
Donna Arlene Low was born on August 25, 1933, in Glenville, Minnesota, the daughter of Clarence and Luella (Freeman) Low. She was a graduate of Fertile High School; a talented athlete, she played basketball. She continued her education at Waldorf College in Forest City. She was united in marriage to Earl Miller on October 28, 1951, in Clear Lake; they were blessed with four children.
Donna was a woman of deep faith, dedicating much of her life to service, family, and community. She began by laboring in the fields picking onions. She worked at Decker, Armour and State Brand. Later, she became a secretary at Miller's Diesel, a role she took great pride in.
Beyond work, Donna cherished the outdoors. She and Earl shared a love for camping and fishing, spending summers in Minnesota and winters in Texas, always eager to make new friends and create lasting memories. A longtime member of the Fertile Church of Christ, she devoted herself to teaching Sunday school and leading
youth group. More recently, she was a member of Celebration Community Church, where her faith continued to be a guiding force in her life. Donna spent the last year and a half at Apple Valley Assisted Living, where she cherished her new friendships.
Above all, Donna's greatest joy was her family. She loved cheering on her grandchildren and great-grandchildren at their school events, always their biggest supporter.
Donna is survived by her children, Sheila (Michael) Ball, Arlyn (Claudia) Miller, Daniel (Penny) Miller, LuAnn (Dick) Paulson; grandchildren, Stefanie (Dean) Black, Staci (John) Scheppler, Angie (Dan) Schmidt, Alicia (Erik) Grimm, Kara (Tom) Kopecky, Krista (Philip) Stec, Heather (Joshua) Schulze, Joshua Miller, Courtney (Chris) Lorenz and Kelsey (Zach) Kuns; numerous great-grandchildren; siblings, Beverly (Ralph) Smith, Eugene (Lois), Low; sisters-in-law and brother in law, Dianne Miller, Eva Miller and Jean (Dan) Blake; along with many nieces and nephews, cousins and her faithful companion dog Lucy.
Donna is preceded in death by her parents Clarence and Luella Low, mother and father-in-law, Verle and Corrine (Zobel) Miller; her husband, Earl Miller; brothers, Clarence 'Junior' Low, Leonard 'Buddy' Low; brothers-in-law Marlin and Jack Miller and Don Gudmonson.
Her family would like to extend their heartfelt gratitude to Oakwood Care Center for the dignified care she received during her brief stay, as well as to St. Croix Hospice for their compassion and support.
Ward Van Slyke Colonial Chapel is in charge of arrangements.

title: Friend of Education: Stacy Doughan
description: Stacy Doughan, Director of the Clear Lake Chamber, was awarded the Clear Lake Education Association's 'Friend of Education' at Clear Lake School's opening day event. Her nomination is as follows:…
content:
Stacy Doughan, Director of the Clear Lake Chamber, was awarded the Clear Lake Education Association's 'Friend of Education' at Clear Lake School's opening day event. Her nomination is as follows:
Stacy always goes above and beyond for our school community. As the President of the Clear Lake Chamber of Commerce, Stacy always thinks of ways for our school activities to get involved. For example, she came up with the idea of having Mario and Pikachu be a part of Thursday's On Main and where we can raise money for our school E-sports program, and dress up as various Disney characters to raise money for our school speech and drama/theater programs. Stacy organizes beginning of the year giveaways by getting local Clear Lake businesses involved and it's a great way to kick off the school year for our staff. Stacy is one of the most warm and caring people in a community that I have ever seen. Stacy's disposition makes her very approachable to talk to and she is always a message or an email away when it comes to volunteering and when it comes to organizing community ideas. Stacey goes above and beyond to make sure Clear Lake is a great place to live, learn, work and play. Category:

title: Betty Jane Theilen
description: Betty Jane Theilen 85, passed away Monday, November 18, 2024, at the Nora Springs Care Center in Nora Springs, surrounded by her loving family. A funeral service was held at 11 a.m. Friday, November…
content:
Betty Jane Theilen 85, passed away Monday, November 18, 2024, at the Nora Springs Care Center in Nora Springs, surrounded by her loving family.
A funeral service was held at 11 a.m. Friday, November 22, at the Fertile Lutheran Church in Fertile; with Pastor Mary Findlay officiating. A viewing was held one hour prior to the service at the church. Burial will take place at Memorial Park Cemetery in Mason City.
In lieu of flowers memorials may be directed to the Fertile Lutheran Church, in Betty's memory.
Betty was born into the loving family of Clyde and Helen (Rahfeldt) Miller in Ames on October 7, 1939. She was the third child in the family of four brothers and three sisters, growing up on the farm and working hard. Betty graduated from Dows High School in 1957 and went on to La'James College of Beauty for Cosmetology where she graduated and also taught as an instructor. She worked many years at Cerro Gordo Beauty Shop and later opened her own salon in her home, Betty's Beauty Shop, in Mason City.
Betty married Orville 'Dean' Theilen, the love of her life, on May 27, 1967 in Minnesota and they were together for 56 years. Betty and Dean spent their lives traveling across the U.S. with their children and family; camping, fishing and sightseeing. They built homes in Mason City, Fertile, Hot Springs, Ark., and helped their kids build their own homes too.
Betty was known for her 'gift of gab', her warm hospitality and exceptional baking (food is love) - zucchini bread, chocolate chip cookies, apple bread and her famous pickles that were beloved by all. She shared all of this as a member of the Fertile Lutheran Church, Fertile Lutheran Sunshine Club, Ladies Aide, her Quilting Club and Fertile Garden Club. She enjoyed various projects with her church family. She made it her mission to know church and community members that were shut-ins or alone, providing her baked goods for them to enjoy.
Betty's true legacy and pride in life are her children, grandchildren and great grandchildren which she spent many years caring for and raising up, teaching them their heritage and love of family traditions while hosting many birthdays and Holiday gatherings with Love. She was often heard singing to them 'You are My Sunshine.'
Betty is survived by her daughter, Sue Neve, of Fertile; son, Paul (Barb) Theilen of Temple, Tex.; grandchildren, Brandon (Kaitlin) Theilen, McKenzie Neve, Trevor (Iris) Neve, Mariah Theilen (Chase), Ryan (Melissa) Rague; great-grandchildren, Lina, Kyler, Bennett, Korbyn, along with baby boy Neve and baby girl Jacobson on the way; siblings Jim (Judy) Miller, Barbara Theilen, Paula Demro, Clyde Jr. (Theresa) Miller; sisters-in-law, Marty Miller, Janie Miller, Millie Schroeder and Clara Howard; along with several special nieces, nephews, cousins and friends.
Betty is preceded in death by her loving husband, Orville 'Dean' Theilen; parents, Clyde and Helen Miller; son, Rick Rague; brothers, Bob Miller and Gerald Miller; mother and father-in-law, Albert and Annie Theilen; brothers and sisters-in-law, Rex Theilen, Ruth (Sherman) Ward, Albert Jr. (Dolly) Theilen, Richard Howard, LaDonna Miller, and Lawrence Schroeder.
Ward Van Slyke is in charge of arrangements.
